title: Answer Engine Optimisation (AEO)
shortDef: AEO is optimising content so answer engines — voice assistants, featured snippets, and AI chat — can pull a direct, accurate answer from your page.
synonyms: AEO, answer optimisation, voice search SEO
content:
Why AEO matters

Answer engines prioritize conciseness, structured facts, and unambiguous question-and-answer patterns. Instead of skimming ten blue links, searchers receive one synthesized response. If your website provides the most structured and authoritative answer, AI models cite your brand as the canonical source.

How to implement AEO

  • Answer the target query directly in the first 40 to 60 words of your section.
  • Use structured markup like FAQPage and QAPage schemas.
  • Keep key business facts, pricing, and definitions identical across all brand profiles.

title: AI Overviews
shortDef: AI Overviews are Google's AI-generated summaries shown above the regular organic results, synthesizing answers and citing authoritative web sources.
content:
How AI Overviews work

Google's Gemini model crawls relevant top-ranking documents, generates a multi-paragraph synthesis answering the user's intent, and shows interactive reference carousel links. Being cited in AI Overviews dramatically multiplies click-through rates compared to standard organic snippets.

title: Backlink
shortDef: A backlink is an incoming hyperlink from an external domain to your website. Quality links from trusted editorial sources signal domain authority and trustworthiness.
synonyms: inbound link, external link, incoming link
content:
Why backlinks remain a foundation of search

Both traditional search algorithms and LLM training corpora evaluate the external citation graph. When reputable industry publications, research papers, and news outlets link to your resources, algorithms calculate higher trust thresholds and brand entity validation.

title: Canonical Tag
shortDef: A canonical tag (rel="canonical") tells search engines which URL represents the master copy of a page when duplicate or similar content exists across multiple URLs.
content:
Preventing duplicate content penalties

Without canonicalization, tracking parameters, sorting filters, and duplicate category paths dilute ranking power and cause indexation bloat. Specifying a canonical link element directs link equity and algorithmic authority to the intended target URL.

title: Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS)
shortDef: CLS measures the visual stability of a web page by tracking unexpected layout shifts during the entire page lifecycle. A score under 0.1 is considered good.
synonyms: CLS, visual stability, Core Web Vitals metric
content:
Why layout shifts hurt user trust

When images load without specified aspect ratios or dynamic fonts swap unexpectedly, buttons and text jump around the screen. This causes accidental clicks, frustrated visitors, and reduced Google page experience rankings.

title: Core Web Vitals
shortDef: Core Web Vitals are Google's essential user-experience metrics: Largest Contentful Paint (loading), Interaction to Next Paint (responsiveness), and Cumulative Layout Shift (stability).
synonyms: CWV, page experience, Google speed benchmarks
content:
The 2026 Core Web Vitals framework

Google's real-world user metrics determine technical eligibility for competitive rankings. The three current core pillars are:

  • LCP (Largest Contentful Paint): Under 2.5 seconds.
  • INP (Interaction to Next Paint): Under 200 milliseconds.
  • CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift): Under 0.1 score.

title: Crawl Budget
shortDef: Crawl budget is the number of URLs search engine bots (like Googlebot) can and want to crawl on your domain within a given timeframe.
synonyms: crawl rate, crawl capacity, bot bandwidth
content:
Maximizing crawl efficiency on large sites

Slow server response times, 404 chains, and parameter duplication drain crawl budget. On programmatic sites with thousands of URLs, keeping response latency under 200ms and pruning thin pages ensures search bots index fresh content immediately.

title: E-E-A-T
shortDef: E-E-A-T stands for Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, and Trustworthiness — the quality criteria Google raters and neural models use to evaluate content credibility.
content:
The four pillars of E-E-A-T

  • Experience: Verifiable first-hand knowledge and real-world testing.
  • Expertise: Formal credentials, technical depth, and demonstrated subject mastery.
  • Authoritativeness: Recognition from industry peers, citations, and awards.
  • Trustworthiness: Transparent business policies, SSL security, cited sources, and contactable authors.

title: Entity SEO
shortDef: Entity SEO is the practice of establishing your brand, executives, and services as unambiguous, interconnected concepts inside search engine and LLM knowledge graphs.
synonyms: knowledge graph SEO, semantic entity optimization
content:
Entities vs keywords

Search engines and generative AI don't just match strings of keywords; they map entities. By publishing complete Organization schema and securing Wikidata, Wikipedia, and Crunchbase profiles, your brand becomes a recognized entity that LLMs cite with certainty.

title: Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO)
shortDef: GEO is the discipline of structuring brand facts, technical schema, and thought leadership so conversational AI systems like ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity cite you.
synonyms: GEO, AI search optimisation, LLM SEO, generative SEO
content:
Why GEO is the future of discovery

Over 40% of technical and B2B buyers now query AI assistants before clicking standard search links. GEO ensures your proprietary methodologies, benchmarks, and solution architectures are quoted word-for-word in LLM answers.

Core GEO principles

  • Answer the search query directly within the initial 50 words.
  • Use JSON-LD structured data to clearly define entity relationships.
  • Earn high-authority citations in datasets that AI models index.
  • Maintain consistent company facts across Crunchbase, LinkedIn, and your homepage.

title: Interaction to Next Paint (INP)
shortDef: INP is Google's Core Web Vitals metric evaluating overall page responsiveness. It measures the latency of user interactions (clicks, taps, keypresses) until visual update.
content:
Understanding INP

In March 2024, INP officially replaced FID (First Input Delay). Unlike FID which only checked the first click, INP tracks the slowest interaction throughout the entire session. A good INP score is 200 milliseconds or less.

title: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP)
shortDef: LCP measures the time it takes for the largest visual element (hero image, video poster, or large text block) in the viewport to become visible. Under 2.5 seconds is good.
synonyms: LCP, load speed metric, page render time
content:
Optimizing LCP

To pass Google's LCP assessment, preload critical hero images, employ modern image formats like AVIF or WebP, and minimize server response time (TTFB). Never lazy-load above-the-fold hero images.

title: llms.txt
shortDef: llms.txt is a standardized plain-text markdown file located at the domain root that provides AI models and web crawlers with a concise, factual summary of the website.
content:
How llms.txt helps AI models discover your site

Much like robots.txt guides web crawlers, llms.txt provides clean, un-rendered Markdown facts and documentation links for AI systems. It reduces token consumption and eliminates hallucination about your services.

title: Local Pack (Map 3-Pack)
shortDef: The local pack is the prominent Google Maps box and top three local business listings displayed for queries with geographic intent (e.g. "SEO company near me").
synonyms: Google 3-pack, map pack, Google Business Profile results
content:
Ranking in the local pack

Local pack positioning is driven by Google Business Profile optimization, geographic proximity, review velocity, and consistent NAP (Name, Address, Phone) citations across local business directories.

title: Programmatic SEO (pSEO)
shortDef: Programmatic SEO is the systematic generation of hundreds or thousands of high-quality, targeted landing pages from structured datasets and dynamic templates.
content:
Scaling organic reach with pSEO

Companies use pSEO to target long-tail search intent at scale, such as city landing pages ("SEO Agency in Austin"), product comparison matrices, or integrations directories. Success requires unique local data, zero-duplicate content, and fast page loads.

title: Schema Markup
shortDef: Schema markup is structured semantic vocabulary (formatted in JSON-LD) added to web code so search engines and AI assistants understand page entities unambiguously.
content:
Why Schema is essential for modern search

Adding Organization, Service, BreadcrumbList, and FAQPage schemas translates human text into machine-readable facts. It unlocks rich snippets in Google and provides clear entity relationships for LLM citation algorithms.

title: Featured Snippet (Position Zero)
shortDef: A featured snippet is a highlighted answer box displayed at the very top of Google's organic search results, extracting a concise paragraph, table, or list from a webpage.
synonyms: position zero, Google answer box, SERP snippet
content:
Winning position zero

Featured snippets capture up to 35% of total search click volume. Winning them requires structuring content with clean H2/H3 question headers followed immediately by direct definitions or bulleted lists.

title: Topical Authority
shortDef: Topical authority is a measure of a website's depth and coverage across a specific subject domain. Search engines prioritize sites that thoroughly cover all subtopics.
synonyms: topic clusters, pillar content, semantic authority
content:
Building impenetrable topical clusters

Instead of isolated blog posts, topical authority relies on pillar pages interconnected with supporting cluster articles. When every adjacent question in your niche is comprehensively addressed, Google rewards the entire domain with top rankings.

title: Zero-Click Search
shortDef: A zero-click search occurs when a user gets their question answered directly on the search engine results page (via AI Overviews, knowledge panels, or snippets) without clicking a link.
synonyms: zero click, SERP answer, direct resolution
content:
Navigating the zero-click landscape

Over 55% of mobile searches now end without a click. To succeed, brands must optimize for brand recall, digital entity footprint, and authoritative citations within AI answers rather than relying solely on raw site traffic.
